motions.item_title: Approve a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming November 30, 2024 as Small Bus…
motions.motion: Councilmember Clark moved to approve a Proclamation of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Proclaiming November 30, 2024 as Small Business Saturday. Councilmember Burnham seconded the motion.
Councilmember Wright moved to approve the consent agenda. Councilmember Wood seconded the motion.

motions.item_title: An Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.25 Residential Zones with the following changes: 1. EMMC 17.25.020(E)(2)(a)(iv) and 17.25.020(F)(1)(a)(iv) are changed to, “Deed Restrictions: A deed restriction shall be recorded for the property dedicated as a moderate income dwelling unit that establishes the unit shall be occupied by the owner and priced for a household with a gross income equal to or less than 80% of the median gross income for Utah County;” and 2. EMMC 17.25.020(E)(2)(a)(i) and 17.25.020(F)(1)(a)(i) are changed to, “Required Amount of Moderate Income Housing: A minimum of 10% of new residential development in this zone shall be dedicated to moderate income housing (MIH) units priced for occupancy by households with a gross income equal to or less than 80% of the median gross income for Utah County per Utah Code 10-9a-103.” Councilmember Gray seconded the motion
motions.motion: Councilmember Wright moved to approve an Ordinance of Eagle Mountain City, Utah, Amending the Eagle Mountain Municipal Code Chapter 17.25 Residential Zones with the following changes: 1. EMMC 17.25.020(E)(2)(a)(iv) and 17.25.020(F)(1)(a)(iv) are changed to, “Deed Restrictions: A deed restriction shall be recorded for the property dedicated as a moderate income dwelling unit that establishes the unit shall be occupied by the owner and priced for a household with a gross income equal to or less than 80% of the median gross income for Utah County;” and 2. EMMC 17.25.020(E)(2)(a)(i) and 17.25.020(F)(1)(a)(i) are changed to, “Required Amount of Moderate Income Housing: A minimum of 10% of new residential development in this zone shall be dedicated to moderate income housing (MIH) units priced for occupancy by households with a gross income equal to or less than 80% of the median gross income for Utah County per Utah Code 10-9a-103.” Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
Councilmember Clark moved that a study of public transit innovation grants be added to the Legislative Priorities List. Councilmember Gray seconded the motion.
